title: Selecting a Vector-Degree Index Set
summary: Using every input index gives the best degree-estimation accuracy but costs exponential time and space; finding a resource-aware selection rule remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the vector numeric mapping applied to a function $g$ with $m$ inputs, determine a suitable rule for selecting the vector-degree index set $I$. Choosing all $m$ input indices, $I=[m]$, is best when only degree-estimation accuracy is considered, but the mapping's time and space complexity are exponential with respect to this set. The unresolved task is to select $I$ so as to retain useful degree-estimation accuracy while controlling both time and space costs.

scope.domain: Vector numeric mapping for degree estimation in correlation cube cryptanalysis.
parameters: m: number of inputs to the function g
I: vector-degree index set controlling the tradeoff between estimation accuracy and resource costs
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine how to choose the index set so that useful degree-estimation accuracy is retained while both time and space costs are controlled.

citations.label: Correlation Cube Attack Revisited:Improved Cube Search and Superpoly Recovery Techniques

progress.summary: The source explicitly asks how to choose the index set, identifies the full set as accuracy-optimal but exponentially costly, and points to heuristic ideas for Trivium rather than a general selection rule.
